enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance). Compared to last month, El Niño strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0°C, extending farther westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean [Fig. 1] . The Niño indices increased, reaching +2.5°C in Niño-3.4, +3.6°C in Niño-3, and +4.4°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained significantly above average [Fig. 3] , associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed conditions persisted over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected the ongoing evolution of El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027 [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
644 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 639 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

 - A slow warm up starts today, despite a cold start. Highs will
   reach the lower 70s in the lowlands on Saturday. We will cool
   back down to near-normal on Sunday.
 
 - Breezy west winds on Saturday, with gusts 25 to 35 mph in the
   lowlands, and a few gusts over 40 mph in the Sacramento 
   Mountains.
 
 - A Pacific cold front arriving towards the middle of next week
   could bring rain and mountain snow chances back to the region.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MST Thu Nov 26 2026

Clear skies and light winds headed into Friday morning. This will
lead to another chilly morning, with lows in the lower-to-mid 30s
across much of Southern New Mexico and Far West Texas. Guidance
keeps the El Paso metro just above the freezing mark, though I
wouldn't be surprised to see portions of Southwest New Mexico and
the rural Rio Grande Valley freeze for a few hours Friday 
morning.

Friday will be warmer, pushing afternoon highs to the mid-to-
upper 60s. This is due to increasing heights aloft ahead of a
strong Pacific high and a light west surface flow. Most of the 
day will be sunny, with a few high clouds spilling down from the 
Four Corners during the evening and overnight hours.

80-knot 500mb jet streak over the Four Corners on Saturday will 
move down the front of the ridge aloft, crossing over Northern 
New Mexico. 995mb lee surface low formation across the Texas
Panhandle will allow for breezy conditions locally Saturday 
afternoon. Not super impressed with the surface pressure gradient
this far south, so west winds 15 to 25 mph with peak gusts to 35
mph is currently the most likely outcome for the I-10/I-25
corridors. Will need to monitor for stronger gusts (40-50 mph) 
over the Sacramento Mountains, which are the only zones relatively
close to Wind Advisory criteria.

Backdoor cold front behind this system will knock temperatures 
back down to normal (lowland highs lower 60s) on Sunday. This 
looks to be a brief cool down and quick rebound headed into next 
week with dry and zonal flow over the region Monday/Tuesday.

GFS and ECMWF deterministic solutions are in good agreement 
resolving a deeper upper low over the Southwestern U.S. sometime 
next week (December 2 to 4). This would be our next shot at 
precipitation chances. Right now, forecast favors Wednesday with
widespread showers across Western New Mexico. This would be 
lowland rain and mountain snow above 7000 feet AGL.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 639 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

VFR conditions with light and variable winds this morning. Winds
will slowly drift towards the west-southwest. Breezier west winds
are expected on Saturday afternoon, with gusts up to 30 knots
possible in the lowlands then.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 639 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026

Temperatures will begin climbing today, but light winds will keep
vent rates mostly in the poor category, with some spots in the
Gila being a little better. 

A weak upper disturbance will graze New Mexico on Saturday, with 
breezy west winds developing. A few gusts over 40 mph will be 
possible in exposed areas in the Sacramento Mountains and the 
Black Range. Lowland deserts may see RH values reach 15% Saturday 
afternoon, but ERC values remain quite low. 

Temperatures will drop back to near normal on Sunday. An upper 
level disturbance and Pacific cold front could bring precip back 
to the area mid-week.
